messages:
ajay: Heads up — we're seeing p99 token latency jump ~2.5x in ap-south-1 on A10 pool after yesterday's release. Canary + prod both affected.

carmen: saw this in dashboards, digging into per-route. Looks correlated with long KV cache misses and increased network retransmits.

li: ran quick flamegraphs on canary; kernel_picker is choosing the `generic_stream` kernel for many L4/A10 RT lanes instead of the `nic_opt` variant. That variant uses less NIC batching so it should have been preferred for this workload.

sofia: can you paste the profiler output?

li: pasting small snippet:

```
perf_top: kernel_picker_select() +45%
kvcache_remote_fetch +30%
net_dev_xmit_retries +18%
spin_wait(affinity) +10%
```

maya: weird — net_dev_xmit_retries suggests NIC saturation / retries. We had a noisy-tenant event on the rack earlier; same hosts flagged by infra.

ajay: CI perf job `runtime-Throughput-A10` also failed for merge 0f3b9c (the batching heuristics PR). Throughput down ~12% on synthetic L4 workload.

perf-bot: [alert] runtime-Throughput-A10: throughput regression 12% on commit 0f3b9c — baseline 9800 tok/s -> 8620 tok/s.

tom: I started a git bisect on the release branch. Suspect change to `batching/heuristics.rs` where we changed kernel selection scoring to include `nic_usage` weight.

ajay: exact repro steps I used:
```
# on canary
export REDWOOD_CLUSTER=ap-south-1-a10
./bench_tokens --model=generation-large --concurrency=64 --seq=512 --duration=300
```

li: bisect result: commit 0f3b9c introduced a bug where `nic_usage` weight defaults to 0.0 when `hw_profile=unavailable` on A10 in our data path, so kernel_picker falls back to generic path.

sofia: summary: kernel choice -> generic kernel -> more per-request NIC bursts -> queueing -> KV cache remote fetches amplify because local hot keys got evicted under burst.

maya: infra confirmed noisy neighbor spike at 03:12 UTC on those hosts (packet drops + transient NIC queue growth). That pushed us over threshold. A10 NICs seem more sensitive in that rack for this pattern.

ajay: mitigation options:
- force kernel_picker to prefer `nic_opt` for A10 in ap-south-1 (hotfix flag)
- lower default concurrency on that pool until kernel selection fixed
- revert 0f3b9c (restore prior heuristics)

carmen: let's try a flag first (non-revert) so we don't affect other regions. Can we patch config and redeploy canaries?

tom: pushed config override: `runtime.kernel_picker.weights.nic_usage=0.8` to ap-south-1 canary. Deploy bot scheduled rolling update.

deploy-bot: deploying runtime-config (kernel_picker override) to ap-south-1 canary — started at 1834568000.

li: after override, quick bench shows p99 back down to ~1.1x baseline in canary. Kernel picker now selects `nic_opt` variant 87% of time.

perf-bot: re-run check: runtime-Throughput-A10 (canary) throughput 9600 tok/s — within 2% of baseline.

sofia: good short-term. We still need to fix the underlying bug in heuristics for `hw_profile=unavailable`. Can someone open a small PR to set a sane default weight?

ajay: I have a draft PR to set default nic_usage weight to 0.5 and add a unit test for the kernel scoring path. Will post link.

maya: infra also recommends adding a NIC saturation alert for A10 clusters (thresholds tuned per region) so noisy neighbors get auto-evicted faster.

carmen: agreed. Also add a perf test to CI that runs a 60s A10 synthetic workload to catch regressions in kernel picker/kv behavior.

tom: note for postmortem: this was a product of three factors: heuristic defaulting + transient noisy neighbor + workload that stresses KV hotset. Individually they'd be fine.

li: can we keep this thread for updates on the PR and revert decision?

ajay: PR is up: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4258 — includes fix + test. I requested review from sofia and tom.

sofia: reviewed, left minor comment. If tests pass, let's merge and schedule a controlled rollout to avoid surprises.

ajay: merged at 1834568360 and started staged rollout to ap-south-1. Monitoring now.

deploy-bot: rollout started for runtime@v2.18.4-fix4258 to ap-south-1 canary at 1834568380.

maya: infra removed noisy tenant from affected hosts at 1834568400.

li: last check: p99 stabilized and KV remote hits dropped ~70% relative to peak.

carmen: closing loop — we won't revert. Action items: add NIC alerts (maya), CI perf test (carmen + ajay), follow-up on kernel telemetry to detect `hw_profile=unavailable` misclassifications (li).

ajay: thanks all :thumbsup:
